To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Class information can be used to enhance the discriminative power of local features by incorporating it into the feature embedding, and that this can be achieved by a supervised Multidimensional scaling (sMDS).".

(i) the use of class information in the feature space improves recognition performance, and (ii) a low dimensional representation of features can provide better results than the original high dimensional representation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem: Given a set of objects, how to design a system that can recognize them from a set of images.

the following question: Given a database of objects, how to obtain a low-dimensional embedding of local feature descriptors, which preserves both class information and the metric structure of the original descriptors.
the problem of how to represent and recognize object classes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed sMDS framework can be applied to any existing local feature descriptor to obtain more robust and discriminative features, which is an important contribution in the field of object recognition.
our method is able to improve the recognition performance by 2-4% on average over the state of the art.
the proposed approach is an interesting and promising new way of combining local features and global object models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sMDS method is able to produce a low dimensional feature representation, where features corresponding to different objects project to different areas, while the local metric relations between features of the same object are still preserved.
the proposed method is able to obtain low dimensional representations of local feature descriptors that are both discriminative and invariant to viewpoint, illumination and clutter.

we have proposed a novel approach to obtain low dimensional representations of local features, which are invariant to the viewpoint, scale, illumination and background clutter, and at the same time, the class information is incorporated into the resulting feature space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of class specific low dimensional feature representations and a simple nearest neighbour classifier is a competitive object recognition approach.
the class specific low dimensional representation of features can be used for both classification and retrieval tasks.
by combining the class information into the low dimensional feature space it is possible to achieve more discriminative feature descriptors.
